---
title: "Single-cell: embeddings"
description: >
  Where cell types, conditions, genes and scores sit on a UMAP:
  DimPlot_bioToolkit(), FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(), orienting an embedding and
  restyling plots made by Seurat.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_common.R")
```

**Question:** where do groups of cells sit on the embedding, and where is a
gene or score high?

| Function | Use |
|---|---|
| `DimPlot_bioToolkit()` | cells coloured by a group (cell type, cluster, condition) |
| `FeaturePlot_bioToolkit()` | cells coloured by a value (gene, QC metric, module score) |
| `transform_embedding()` | flip or rotate an embedding to a conventional orientation |
| `format_sc_plots()`, `manipulate_sc_plot()`, `add_dimension_arrows()` | restyle plots made by Seurat, scCustomize, SCpubr ... |

Both plot functions keep Seurat's arguments (`group.by`, `split.by`,
`features`, `reduction`, `cells`, `cols`, `pt.size`, `label`) and draw panels
of a fixed size, with dimension arrows in place of axes.

**Data:** 8,000 PBMCs from [Kang et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4042),
8 donors, control or interferon-β (IFN-β) for 6 h; log-normalized, Harmony
integration over condition, UMAP; the authors' cell type labels.

```{r data}
pbmc <- docs_kang()
pbmc
head(pbmc[[]], 3)
```

## Cells by group

```{r dimplot}
DimPlot_bioToolkit(pbmc, group.by = "cell_type", label = TRUE)
```

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### `split.by`

One panel per level of a second variable; all panels share one legend and
one size.

```{r dim-split}
DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    panel.width = 3
)
```

#### `cells.highlight`

Colour some cells and draw the rest in grey, e.g. one cell type:

```{r dim-highlight}
mono <- colnames(pbmc)[pbmc$cell_type %in% c("CD14 Mono", "FCGR3A Mono")]
DimPlot_bioToolkit(pbmc, group.by = "cell_type", cells.highlight = mono)
```

#### `cells`

Plot a subset only. `full.extent = TRUE` keeps the axes of the whole object,
so that the subset lines up with the full plot:

```{r dim-cells}
DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    cells = mono,
    full.extent = TRUE
)
```

#### `outline`

An outline around the cell clouds; `outline.color = "darken"` uses a darker
shade of each group's colour.

```{r dim-outline}
DimPlot_bioToolkit(pbmc, group.by = "cell_type", outline = TRUE)
```

#### `mark`

Colour by a fine annotation and outline a broader one (`mark.by`) with a
dashed line around each cloud. Cells with no `mark.by` group (here the few,
scattered megakaryocytes) are not outlined:

```{r dim-mark}
lineage <- c(
    "CD4 T" = "Lymphoid",
    "CD8 T" = "Lymphoid",
    "NK" = "Lymphoid",
    "B" = "Lymphoid",
    "CD14 Mono" = "Myeloid",
    "FCGR3A Mono" = "Myeloid",
    "DC" = "Myeloid",
    "Megakaryocyte" = NA
)
pbmc$lineage <- factor(
    unname(lineage[as.character(pbmc$cell_type)]),
    levels = c("Lymphoid", "Myeloid")
)
DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    mark = TRUE,
    mark.by = "lineage",
    mark.cols = c("grey30", "#B5338A")
)
```

#### Legend

`legend.position` takes "right", "left", "top", "bottom", "inside" (in the
empty corner of the panel) or "none".

```{r dim-legend}
DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "condition",
    legend.position = "inside",
    cols = c("grey60", "#B5338A")
)
```

### Integration and the embedding

The default `reduction` is "umap". This object also holds the UMAP computed
before integration: stimulated and control cells were captured separately and
IFN-β changes the expression of every cell type, so without integration the
two conditions form separate clouds. Any reduction of the object can be
plotted:

```{r dim-reduction}
DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "condition",
    reduction = "umap.unintegrated",
    cols = c("grey60", "#B5338A")
)
```

### Where the arrows go {.tabset .tabset-pills}

With several panels, the dimension arrows are drawn once, in the bottom left
panel, by default. `arrow.panels` puts them in every panel, or in the panels
along one edge of the grid: `"left"` / `"right"` (the first / last panel of
each row) and `"top"` / `"bottom"` (the top / lowest panel of each column). In
a grid whose last row is incomplete, a panel with nothing below it is on the
bottom edge. The same argument works in `FeaturePlot_bioToolkit()`,
`DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit()` and `format_sc_plots()`.

#### `"bottom.left"`

```{r arrows-bl}
DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "donor",
    ncol = 3,
    panel.width = 1.6,
    legend.position = "none"
)
```

#### `"left"`

```{r arrows-left}
DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "donor",
    ncol = 3,
    panel.width = 1.6,
    legend.position = "none",
    arrow.panels = "left"
)
```

#### `"bottom"`

```{r arrows-bottom}
DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "donor",
    ncol = 3,
    panel.width = 1.6,
    legend.position = "none",
    arrow.panels = "bottom"
)
```

#### `"all"`

```{r arrows-all}
DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "donor",
    ncol = 3,
    panel.width = 1.6,
    legend.position = "none",
    arrow.panels = "all"
)
```

### Arrow size

The arrows keep the same proportion to the panel at any size: 2 cm long on a
3.5-inch panel, and scaled with the panel's shorter side, labels included.
Small panels get small arrows that stay clear of the cells near the edges,
large panels larger ones. `arrow.scale` makes them larger or smaller at any
panel size (default 1); it works in every function that draws the arrows.

```{r arrow-scale}
DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    panel.width = 2,
    legend.position = "none",
    arrow.scale = 1.3
)
```

## Genes and scores

```{r featureplot}
FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = c("CD3E", "MS4A1", "CD14", "FCGR3A"),
    ncol = 2,
    panel.width = 2.5
)
```

Cells with no expression (0) are drawn in grey, apart from the colour scale,
so that "not detected" is not confused with "low" (`na.cutoff = "auto"`).
Gene names are set in italics.

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### `split.by`

One gene across conditions, on one shared scale (`keep.scale = "feature"`):
*ISG15*, an interferon-stimulated gene, is induced in every cell type.

```{r feat-split}
FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "ISG15",
    split.by = "condition",
    panel.width = 3
)
```

#### Module score

Scores centred on 0 get a diverging scale automatically (`diverging = "auto"`):
the centre colour stays at 0 and each side reaches its full colour at its own
extreme, so a score from -0.2 to 1.5 is not faded on the negative side. Here,
Seurat's `AddModuleScore()` on the MSigDB Hallmark interferon-α response
genes (IFN-α and IFN-β signal through the same receptor and induce the same
genes):

```{r feat-score}
# msigdbr::msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "H"), cached
hallmark <- docs_hallmark()
is_ifn <- hallmark$gs_name == "HALLMARK_INTERFERON_ALPHA_RESPONSE"
ifn_genes <- intersect(hallmark$gene_symbol[is_ifn], rownames(pbmc))
pbmc <- Seurat::AddModuleScore(
    pbmc,
    features = list(ifn_genes),
    name = "IFN_alpha_score",
    seed = 1
)
FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "IFN_alpha_score1",
    split.by = "condition",
    panel.width = 3,
    legend.title = "IFN-α\nresponse"
)
```

#### Metadata

Any metadata column, e.g. a QC metric; `max.cutoff` caps the scale at a
quantile so that a few extreme cells do not compress it:

```{r feat-meta}
FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "nCount_RNA",
    max.cutoff = "q99",
    cols = "viridis"
)
```

#### `label`

Label groups (active identities, or `label.by`) on top of the values:

```{r feat-label}
FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "CD14",
    label = TRUE,
    label.by = "cell_type"
)
```

### Sparse genes: `geom` {.tabset .tabset-pills}

Most cells have zero counts for many genes, even where the gene is expressed
(dropout). Three ways to draw them, here for the chemokine *CXCL10*, induced by
interferon in monocytes:

#### `"point"`

Every cell coloured by its own value (default).

```{r geom-point}
cxcl10 <- colnames(pbmc)[pbmc$condition == "IFN-beta"]
FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "CXCL10",
    cells = cxcl10,
    panel.width = 3
)
```

#### `"hex"`

Cells binned into hexagons. `hex.fun = "mean"` colours by the mean value in a
tile (zeros included); `hex.fun = "pct"` by the % of cells expressing it.

```{r geom-hex}
FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "CXCL10",
    cells = cxcl10,
    geom = "hex",
    hex.fun = "pct",
    panel.width = 3
)
```

#### `"density"`

Values smoothed over neighbouring cells. `density.method = "smooth"` (a
kernel-weighted mean, in the units of the feature); `"wkde"` is the weighted
kernel density of the Nebulosa package, scaled to a maximum of 1.

```{r geom-density}
FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "CXCL10",
    cells = cxcl10,
    geom = "density",
    panel.width = 3
)
```

## Orienting an embedding

UMAP coordinates have no meaningful direction. `transform_embedding()` flips
and / or rotates (`rotate`, in degrees) a 2-D reduction in the object, for
display only (distances are unchanged), e.g. to keep the orientation of a
published figure:

```{r transform}
pbmc_t <- transform_embedding(pbmc, reduction = "umap", flip_vertical = TRUE)
DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc_t,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    label = TRUE,
    panel.width = 3
)
```

## Restyling plots made by Seurat

`format_sc_plots()` applies the same look to plots made by other packages:
axes replaced by dimension arrows (by default on the bottom left plot only;
`arrow.panels` as above), legends removed or moved, and the plots arranged in
a grid. It also takes plots made separately with `DimPlot_bioToolkit()` or
`FeaturePlot_bioToolkit()`: the arrows they have are replaced, so that each
plot keeps at most one set.

```{r format-seurat, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4}
seurat_plots <- list(
    Seurat::DimPlot(pbmc, group.by = "cell_type", reduction = "umap"),
    Seurat::FeaturePlot(pbmc, features = "ISG15", reduction = "umap")
)
format_sc_plots(seurat_plots, ncol = 2)
```

```{r format-own}
own_plots <- list(
    DimPlot_bioToolkit(pbmc, group.by = "cell_type", panel.width = 2.2),
    FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(pbmc, features = "ISG15", panel.width = 2.2)
)
format_sc_plots(own_plots, ncol = 2, arrow.panels = "all")
```

For a single plot, `add_dimension_arrows()` adds the arrows and
`manipulate_sc_plot()` changes its axes, legend or grid:

```{r arrows-seurat, fig.width = 4.5, fig.height = 4}
p <- Seurat::DimPlot(pbmc, group.by = "condition", reduction = "umap")
p <- manipulate_sc_plot(p, remove.grid = TRUE, legend.title = "Condition")
add_dimension_arrows(p, reduction = "umap", arrow.scale = 0.8)
```

Plots made by Seurat have no fixed panel size, so give `save_plot()` a
`width` and `height` in inches; the arrows are scaled with the panel size
they are drawn at. Arguments of these three functions were
renamed to dot.case in 0.10.0; `add.arrow` and `bottom.left.only` of
`format_sc_plots()` were replaced by `arrow.panels` in 1.0.0. The old names
still work, with a deprecation warning.
